key_insight: Input-only prompt optimization can strongly suppress some internal “evaluation-awareness” latents, but linear readout of a latent does not guarantee causal control over the model’s behavior.
engineering_relevance: This suggests safety probes and evaluation-aware detectors should not be treated as reliable control levers, because fluent prompt edits can erase or mimic internal signals without consistently changing downstream judgments.
method: Use input-side optimization (GCG-style token search + self-cross-entropy fluency regularizer) to minimize a targeted latent toward zero.
Sweep fluency weight to balance suppression against prompt naturalness.
Test five target types across Llama-3.2-3B and Llama-3.1-8B: CAA direction, subspace norm, SAE feature, MLP neuron, and behavioral logit.
evidence_signal: Across models, the targeted latent was robustly suppressible (around z≈-7), a causally validated SAE feature could be selectively turned off, but a held-in-context eval-direction did not reduce behavioral eval judgment and sometimes slightly increased it.
watch_item: A major limitation is that suppressing a readout direction can fail to change behavior—and may even track placebo effects—so apparent latent control may not reflect genuine causal intervention.
paper_title: Minimizing Targeted Activations: Input-Only Suppression of Evaluation-Awareness Latents in Large Language Models
